In 2025, Ty France was a light-hitting first baseman who won a Gold Glove with the Twins (and Blue Jays) and didn’t generate much interest in the 25-26 offseason. In his time with the Twins, France only managed a 0.8 WAR, 6 homers, and an 89 OPS+. However, France was unlucky per his xwOBA through the entire 2025 season, as it was 26 points higher than his actual wOBA. In fact, his xwOBA in 2025 was a point higher than it was in 2026.

One thing that could have contributed to his comeback season is the fact he was pulling the ball in the air a lot more than he was with the Twins (6% difference). France probably won’t replicate what he did in 2026 again, but there’s a happy medium between what he did in 2025 and in 2026 offensively.

He won’t get an enormous deal, but for the right price at a two-year deal, the Twins might be able to strike a deal with one of the good bats on the market in France.
